newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Miners depress Australian stocks at opening.
newsitem.headline: Miners depress Australian stocks at opening.

text.p: The Australian share market eased at the opening on Monday, weighed down by market heavyweight Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd which eased on first quarter results released on Friday and a weakening copper price.
The All Ordinaries index was down 7.8 points at 2233.0 in early trading.
With a mixed performance on overseas markets, traders chose to focus on commodity prices, particularly copper, which again took a beating in London trading.
"BHP led the way down but most commodity-related stocks are down," said dealer Peter Struk of brokerage Reynolds and Co.
Struk said that while BHP's first quarter results were now built into the share price the fall looked to be overdone and there was the possibility of some recovery later in the day.
"The result is pretty much built into the price and the market is now focussed on offshore," he said.
Other traders said the BHP share price was likely to remain skittish as long as the copper price remained volatile.
Falls outnumbered rises by a ratio of about three to two, while about 42 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
BHP was down 27 cents at A$15.77 in early trade. Miner CRA, ex-dividend 20.65 cents, was down 33 cents at A$18.12.
